objective: добиться отзывчивости microsoft rdp, сохранив качество и скорость воспроизведения графики/клипов и завершить план

changes.pixel_history: Protocol 7: a PATCH may reference the exact pixels of earlier records by distance in a 4 M pixel ring. Text tiles cost about a quarter on the wire. Record order is strict per viewer, and any inconsistency disables the layer rather than painting wrong pixels.
changes.cursor_cache: A cursor image is cropped to its visible pixels and defined once per viewer. Compositors hand out a 64x64 buffer (22 KB encoded) and alternate a few images under new ids.
changes.stamp_packets: A packet of at most 256 bytes pays pacer debt but does not wait behind it. Holding nearly empty pictures overflowed the four-picture queue, whose repair was an independent picture of 80-100 KB over text.
changes.shared_capacity: A cut of the video target adds what exact records recently took of the path to the rate delivered to video. Idle video beside busy tiles had stated 663 kbit/s on a 2 Mbit/s path.
changes.reply_spacing: The viewer replies to records at most every 10 ms. One reply per record plus the SCTP acknowledgement it drew cost a narrow path more than a small record does.
changes.vaapi_uncropped: VA-API uses VBR and QP floor 20 for an uncropped picture while regions are on. AMD otherwise spent all 8 Mbit/s on a static picture when no crop had been selected (84 MB per bench profile, about 1 run in 12).
changes.output_refresh: On a wlroots source the worker asks for twice the capture rate on the output, up to 240 Hz; capture still starts at most at the requested rate. KWin nested in sway and the capture each wait for that output next frame.
changes.key_input_response: A key press arms the same immediate, unfenced first change per tile as a pointer event. The first key after a focus change had no exact tile of the current layout to replace early, and waited for its video picture: 104-173 ms against 26-60 ms for the following keys.
changes.idle_video_rate: With history, the worker rate for strips and input responses ignores the video target while no tile is busy. Only a delivery rate reported from acknowledgement delay binds it. Video has its own TCP connection, so its target could still reach 604 kbit/s on a 2 Mbit/s path.
changes.video_envelope: A window dragged across the screen widens the video plane and stays a plane that follows the path. Only motion that itself covers 80% of the desktop for a second selects the whole picture, for at least 5 s. It flipped between the two every 1-5 s before, with an independent picture each way and 8 Mbit/s of codec rate on a path of 990 kbit/s.
changes.band_waits_with_history: With history a late strip waits for bandwidth up to 2 s, re-encoded fresh, instead of being handed to video and then repainted, with a clear each way.
changes.flight_window_from_delivery: When a queue is seen the exact window goes directly to what the path delivers in a round trip, rather than losing a third per round.

findings: First drag motion at 2 Mbit/s was 151 ms against 84 ms at 20 Mbit/s because a 22-26 KB cursor definition went out ahead of the first copy, measured on the wire with a proxy trace. KWin changes the cursor at each drag, and any hover over an edge or text does the same.

Reducing the flight margin from 32 to 20 ms at high RTT did not move the clip peak (552 against 553 ms) and lowered hard-cut SSIM to 0.898-0.903 and narrow fps from 51 to 48-49. It was reverted. A trace of the 32 ms margin on a low-RTT link is what an existing test protects.

The clip source-age peak is at the first bandwidth cut: 70-80 KB already in flight plus a 40-48 KB refresh picture. Deferring the refresh cannot help, because age is measured on each displayed frame and a frozen picture ages equally.

Over a text backdrop at 2 Mbit/s the wire stayed full while records took a third of it. Replies and the SCTP acknowledgements they drew were most of the difference: spacing them moved the median drag lag from 106 to 59 ms.
RDP is polled at 1-2 ms on X11, the QSM observer at 16.7 ms by rAF, so about 8 ms of the remaining first-response gap is measurement.

The Firefox burst update gap of about 1500 ms is the bench: the span of notches itself grows from 966 to 2500 ms while rAF stays regular, and Chromium never shows it. A wheel call blocks in Playwright for Firefox.

120 Hz on the sway output took about 15 ms off every first response on the PVE container lane, more than the two half-periods expected, and clip gates held. It made no measurable difference on the AMD lane, whose click overhead over the round trip was already about 12 ms at 60 Hz; typing there stays about 33 ms behind clicks and is unexplained. VM sources are unaffected by this change.

A bad path alone does not prevent startup: under stalls of 0.5-3 s every 2-8 s from before page load, video started, every key arrived and all snapshots arrived late but complete. So TCP stalls do not explain the two Mac sessions in which video did not start.

At a target of 604 kbit/s tiles could not keep up over text at 2 Mbit/s and 100 ms, handed over to video and grew the crop, and a drag stayed visibly stuck mid-way for up to 3.4 s after release. After the idle-video rate change the final position error is 0 and settling fell from 186 to 98 ms.

One native QSV run of exp208 exceeded the source-age excess limit (450 ms) because its first target cut came 12 s into the narrow phase instead of the usual 1.4-1.6 s. Repeats gave 277 and 246, and exp209 gave 263. It is 1 of 10 QSV runs and its cause is not established.

On Mac a run of exp207 showed 42.9 fps with no overflows. When the path was calm exp208 and exp209 reached 54-55 fps, and for the first time since Nov 4 the whole lifecycle including a hidden tab passed. So the low figure was the path. A same-hour A/B was skipped automatically because the path was bad at that moment.
The 120 Hz output cost almost nothing in the guest: KWin 0.054 to 0.060 cores and sway 0.010 to 0.013 cores across a bench.

The VM path is 35-55 ms behind the container path on the same route: typing 164-170 ms against 118-120 ms at a round trip of about 115 ms. The first exact record arrives 138-184 ms after a key and the viewer adds about 10 ms, so the difference is in the guest and QEMU, and frame readback averages only 3.2 ms. Asking for 120 Hz has no effect there: QEMU Display1 has no refresh in SetUIInfo and the guest stays at the EDID default of 75 Hz.

The container fixtures have no window shadow, the VM desktop has the Breeze one. Over text a moving shadow gives new blended pixels each frame, which neither copy nor history can reuse: 358 bytes per record against 137, and about 1 MB/s for a drag. So the container text results are optimistic for a desktop with shadows.

A 31 minute session was stable: no errors, exact layer enabled, one epoch, 554 M history pixels (about 130 times the ring) with no checksum mismatch, worker at 200 MB, JS heap at 24-26 MB, latencies flat. Bridge RSS grew from 331 to 785 MB, but with the lab probe storing nothing it stayed at 273-305 MB over 18 minutes, so that growth is the probe.
corrections: A candidate version bump changed the literal window coordinate 204 to 205 in the native harness, so both native runs of exp205 failed an assertion before measuring. They are kept as w1 and were rerun as w2 with the coordinate restored; the only damaged literal was found by normalized diffs against exp204.
An earlier note in this session attributed the Mac glyph spikes to flow control. An A/B with exp190 and an idle path probe showed the network path instead.
limits: Launch/ACL mocked; dedicated guests only. Exact UI stays off by default; these results apply only with it enabled.
RDP client is FreeRDP on X11, not mstsc. Different OS, toolkit, compositor and encoder: not a single-variable backend comparison.
Text behind a moved window was run on QSM only: the RDP column is its flat backdrop.
Small run counts: 2 Chromium rounds, 1 text round and 1 Firefox round per candidate.
Text over a 2 Mbit/s path remains behind flat on AMD at a higher round trip: median drag lag 214-368 ms and one final error of 114 px.
The clip excess gate of 400 ms is within spread of the PVE runs. Across exp204-213, 2 of 19 runs exceeded it, at 416 and 401 ms.

A VM desktop with shadows and text behind a window stays weak at 2 Mbit/s: median drag lag 305-475 ms, and the first drag after the path narrows can stay stuck mid-way past the end of the measurement.
exp213 was not run on the Mac because its path was bad at that time; the Mac figures are exp209. Long-session figures are exp209 too.
No RDP run exists with text or shadows behind a window, and RDP was not measured against a VM guest here.

open_findings.mac_input_stop: On one Mac run of exp202 input snapshots and a key stopped reaching the bridge at the moment of a 1.5 s frame gap while the page stayed visible, focused and rendering, and the control channel was not closed. Not reproduced: 50 of 50 keys and all snapshots survived artificial stalls of 0.4-3.5 s on PVE, and no other session of 436 shows it. Data channels have their own DTLS and TURN/TCP connection, so a backed-off TCP connection is the leading untested explanation. A soak with per-transport and socket diagnostics is ready but could not run: the Mac path had p90 1.4-2 s and spikes up to 15 s with no session.
open_findings.mac_startup: On the degraded Mac path video did not start within 50 s in 2 attempts, with 35-185 keyframe requests. An emulated path with TCP stalls does not reproduce it (see startup_under_path_storm), so the cause is still unknown.
open_findings.ice_failures_amd: Two of 4 AMD runs of exp203 lost ICE at about 380 s of session age, in the same profile, while the shared WAN route showed spikes. No failure in the following 24 runs of exp203-209, so it was not reproduced.
open_findings.qsv_late_first_cut: See findings: 1 of 10 QSV runs, first cut 12 s late.

responsiveness_text_behind_window_chromi.scope: Same bench with text behind the moved window: QSM only, RDP was not run on it.

responsiveness_asrock_amd_vaapi.scope: Controller to host TCP RTT is about 85 ms against 0.25 ms for PVE, so absolute values are not comparable with RDP at equal netem delay.

startup_under_path_storm.scope: PVE, Chromium, 45 ms delay, stalls of 0.5-3 s every 2-8 s from before the page loads, 2 sessions of 120 s on exp206.
startup_under_path_storm.note: A row flagged by the detector is snapshots delayed by a stall: totals sent and received matched exactly at the end of both sessions.

mac_chrome_real_path.scope: Real Chrome 156 on macOS through the actual PVE TCP/8006 path. Glyph limit 600 ms, source fps limit 45.
